st: Pat the fish dry and cut a few deep slashes on each side.
Mash the tamarind with [[3 tbsp]] water, then mix in the chilies, garlic, lime juice, [[1 tbsp]] oil and salt.
Rub the marinade into the slashes and inside the cavity.
Cover and marinate in the fridge.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush with [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Grill the fish until the skin is charred and the flesh flakes easily.
Turn once carefully and cook the other side.
Top with basil and serve with rice and a wedge of lime.
Drain the soaked corn and put it in a pot with [[5 cups]] water.
Bring to a boil and then simmer until the corn is almost tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic until golden.
Add the mung beans to the corn pot.
Simmer until the beans are soft.
Add the pumpkin and onion mixture, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Cook until the pumpkin is tender and the stew is thick, mashing a few pieces to thicken.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot.

ing: for wrapping, in place of bamboo
st: Mix the lemongrass, chilies, garlic, ginger, turmeric, oil and salt into a thick paste.
Rub the paste well into the goat meat.
Cover and marinate in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Traditional tukir is cooked in bamboo over a fire; a sealed packet gives a similar result.
Wrap the meat tightly in banana leaves and then foil, or use a lidded roasting dish.
Roast slowly until the meat is very tender and nearly falling off the bone.
Unwrap and check the meat has reached at least 145°F (63°C), though it should be much more tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with rice and chili.
Drain the soaked beans and rinse. Put them in a pot with [[8 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaves.
Boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer until tender. Boiling is important to cook kidney beans safely.
Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the pork on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes and paprika and cook until they break down.
Add the sausage and the pork mixture to the beans.
Add the salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered, stirring, until the pork is tender and the stew is thick.
Taste, adjust seasoning and serve with rice.

ing: or banana leaf squares and string
st: Soak the rice in water and drain.
If using palm leaves, weave them into small pouches, or fold banana leaf into small squares and tie.
Mix the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt.
Fill each pouch about half full with rice. The rice will expand.
Close the pouches tightly.
Place them in a large pot, cover with the coconut mixture and extra water, and boil.
Check the water level now and then and add hot water to keep the pouches covered.
Cool slightly, unwrap, and serve sliced with meat dishes.
Dice the tomatoes and place in a bowl.
Finely dice the onion and add it.
Chop the chilies and add them, using more or less to taste.
Pour in the lime juice and sprinkle with salt.
Stir in the chopped mint.
Let it rest so the flavors blend.
Serve with grilled fish or meat.
Remove the stems of the chilies and chop them roughly. Wear gloves if you can.
Peel the garlic cloves and trim the ends.
Pound the chilies and garlic in a mortar to a coarse paste, or pulse in a small processor.
Stir in the salt until it is evenly mixed.
Mix in the lime juice and stir well.
Heat the oil until warm and pour over the paste, stirring.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge.
